response: Etoricoxib, a selective COX-2 inhibitor, has been shown to be effective in preventing heterotopic ossification (HO) after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). Studies have demonstrated that etoricoxib can reduce the incidence and severity of HO when used as a prophylactic measure. Its efficacy is thought to be due to its ability to inhibit the inflammatory process that contributes to the formation of heterotopic bone. As a result, etoricoxib is considered a viable option for preventing HO in patients undergoing primary THA.
